rules.statement: In a background worker loop, treat an OperationCanceledException as shutdown only when the host's stopping token is actually cancelled; handle any other cancellation (such as an HttpClient timeout) as an ordinary failure of that unit of work.
rules.why: A timeout surfaces as a TaskCanceledException whose token is not the worker's. A loop that treats every cancellation as shutdown ends on it, and BackgroundServiceExceptionBehavior.StopHost then stops the whole host.
rules.check: Look for `catch (OperationCanceledException)` or `catch (TaskCanceledException)` in BackgroundService/ExecuteAsync loops that break or return without a `when (stoppingToken.IsCancellationRequested)` filter or an equivalent check.

rules.statement: Validate options when the host starts: register an IValidateOptions validator with ValidateOnStart that rejects out-of-range values (for example counts or capacities below 1) and names the configuration key of each invalid value.
rules.why: A bad value such as a queue that holds nothing or a worker that runs nothing should stop the host at startup, not silently drop or never run work.
rules.check: New options classes with numeric limits or enum values that are not covered by a validator, are registered without `.ValidateOnStart()`, or whose failure messages leave out the configuration key.

rules.statement: When an options property is an enum bound from configuration, validate that its value is a defined member of the enum (for example with Enum.IsDefined) and fail startup if it is not.
rules.why: A value that names no member of the enum, such as for BoundedChannelFullMode, has to stop the host instead of causing undefined behavior at runtime.
rules.check: Enum-typed options properties whose validator does not check for a defined value.

rules.statement: Create one service scope per unit of background work with `CreateAsyncScope` (`await using`), and resolve every handler for that unit of work from that one scope.
rules.why: Scoped handlers then get their dependencies per attempt, and the scope is disposed asynchronously.
rules.check: `IServiceScopeFactory.CreateScope()` or `IServiceProvider.CreateScope()` in async background processing code, a scope that is not disposed with `await using`, or handlers resolved from the root provider.

rules.statement: When a job has several handlers, run them all in sequence even if one fails, and reschedule the job at most once per failed attempt no matter how many handlers failed.
rules.why: If each failing handler scheduled its own retry, one failed attempt would run again as many times as handlers failed.
rules.check: Retry or reschedule calls inside a per-handler loop or catch block, or a handler failure that skips the remaining handlers.

rules.statement: Process a queue of independent background jobs with a bounded number of concurrent consumers (for example several loops reading one Channel created with SingleReader = false), not a single serial loop and not Parallel.ForEachAsync.
rules.why: With a single loop, one slow endpoint holds up every queued job. With Parallel.ForEachAsync, an exception in one body cancels every running job.
rules.check: Job-dispatch workers that run one job at a time with a single reader loop, that use Parallel.ForEachAsync over a channel, or that read one channel from several consumers while it is created with SingleReader = true.

rules.statement: Make job handlers idempotent, and make any job handler registered as a singleton thread-safe.
rules.why: A retry runs every handler of the job again, and several consumers can run a singleton handler at the same time.
rules.check: Job handlers with non-idempotent side effects that a retry would repeat, or singleton handlers that keep mutable state without synchronization.
